Class ApiKeyAuthenticationProvider

java.lang.Object
org.jwcarman.who.apikey.ApiKeyAuthenticationProvider
All Implemented Interfaces:
org.springframework.security.authentication.AuthenticationProvider
public class ApiKeyAuthenticationProvider extends Object implements org.springframework.security.authentication.AuthenticationProvider
Signs in with an API key: checks the key's shape, looks it up by its hash, refuses it once expired, and resolves it to an active identity whose permissions are cut down to the key's scopes. A key's use is recorded at most once per interval; a failure to record it is logged and never refuses the key.

The raw key is erased from the request token as soon as it is hashed, so it reaches no event, exception or log line; neither does its hash.

A key that signs in returns a WhoAuthenticationToken with SignInMethod.API_KEY and publishes no who event: a key authenticates every request, and Spring Security's AuthenticationSuccessEvent already reports each one.

Every refusal is the same BadCredentialsException ("Invalid API key"). It publishes SignInFailed with SignInFailureReason.UNKNOWN_KEY when the key has the wrong shape or checksum (without a lookup), is unknown, revoked or linked to no identity, SignInFailureReason.EXPIRED_KEY once it has expired, or SignInFailureReason.INACTIVE_IDENTITY when its identity is not active, and logs one DEBUG line. A fault looking the key up propagates.

Not a bean: an AuthenticationProvider bean would join the application's global authentication manager. ApiKeyAuthenticationFilter uses it.

      public ApiKeyAuthenticationProvider(ApiKeyCredentialRepository apiKeyCredentialRepository, WhoService whoService, ApiKeyFormat format, Duration lastUsedInterval, WhoEventPublisher eventPublisher, Clock clock)
      Creates the provider.
      Parameters:
      apiKeyCredentialRepository - looks keys up by their hash and records their use
      whoService - resolves a key to its identity
      format - checks a key's shape before any lookup
      lastUsedInterval - how often, at most, a key's use is recorded; positive
      eventPublisher - where refusals are published
      clock - decides expiry and stamps events and use
      Throws:
      IllegalArgumentException - if lastUsedInterval is not positive
